name: CAPSTONE
short_status: All primary and extended mission objectives achieved; NASA activities concluded June 2026 after nearly four years; Advanced Space continues flying it as a commercial testbed in the NRHO (as of July 2026).
tagline: Advanced Space for NASA · United States · Orbiter · 2022 · Commercial and multipolar Success
stats: spacecraft ever to fly a near-rectilinear halo orbit, the orbit planned for Gateway
12U CubeSat, about the size of a microwave oven
per lap of the 9:2 resonant NRHO, from about 1,600 km over the north pole to 70,000 km beyond the south
NASA contract to Advanced Space for the spacecraft and operations, plus $9.95M to Rocket Lab for launch

facts.label: Launch
facts.value: 28 June 2022, on a Rocket Lab Electron from Launch Complex 1, Mahia, New Zealand

facts.label: Ownership
facts.value: Designed and built by Terran Orbital (Tyvak); owned and operated by Advanced Space of Westminster, Colorado, for NASA

facts.label: Contract
facts.value: $13.7 million SBIR Phase III award to Advanced Space (September 2019) to develop and operate the mission

facts.label: Launch contract
facts.value: $9.95 million to Rocket Lab (February 2020), originally slated for Wallops, Virginia, later moved to New Zealand

facts.label: Spacecraft
facts.value: 12U CubeSat, 25 kg, 34 x 34 x 64 cm, with eight 0.25-newton hydrazine thrusters giving over 200 m/s of delta-V

facts.label: Transfer
facts.value: Four-month ballistic lunar transfer: Rocket Lab's Lunar Photon fired seven times over six days, raising its orbit's high point to around 810,000 miles from Earth, before releasing CAPSTONE on 4 July 2022

facts.label: Orbit
facts.value: Near-rectilinear halo orbit passing about 1,000 miles over the lunar north pole and out to 43,500 miles past the south pole, one lap every six and a half days

facts.label: NRHO insertion
facts.value: Insertion burn at 7:39 p.m. EST on 13 November 2022, followed by two clean-up maneuvers; first spacecraft to fly an NRHO and first CubeSat to operate at the Moon

facts.label: Primary mission
facts.value: Completed 18 May 2023, after six months in the NRHO: 28 orbits, 7 maneuvers, 6 lunar eclipses endured

facts.label: CAPS demonstration
facts.value: Five successful crosslink ranging demonstrations with Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, the first on 9 May 2023, plus one-way ranging using an onboard chip-scale atomic clock

facts.label: Extended mission
facts.value: 15-month NASA extension managed by the SCaN Division: first lunar test of autoNGC autonomous navigation and first flight of the latest delay/disruption tolerant networking protocols beyond Earth orbit

facts.label: Mission end
facts.value: NASA activities concluded in June 2026 with all primary and extended objectives achieved; Advanced Space continues to use the spacecraft as a technology development testbed (as of July 2026)

timeline: NASA awards Advanced Space a $13.7 million SBIR Phase III contract to fly a CubeSat pathfinder to Gateway's planned orbit
Rocket Lab wins the $9.95 million launch contract, then planned from Wallops Island, Virginia
Launch on an Electron from Mahia, New Zealand; the Lunar Photon upper stage begins six days of orbit-raising burns
Lunar Photon's seventh and final burn releases CAPSTONE onto its four-month ballistic lunar transfer, a low-energy route that lets the Sun's gravity carry the CubeSat to the Moon on minimal fuel
4 to 6 Jul 2022
The radio falls silent hours after separation, knocked out by an improperly formatted command; onboard fault protection eventually clears the fault and contact is re-established on July 6
A partially open thruster valve during a trajectory correction spins the spacecraft up beyond what its reaction wheels can counter; CAPSTONE tumbles in deep space for a month
Recovery commands stop the spin and restore full three-axis control, keeping the arrival date intact
Insertion burn at 7:39 p.m. EST makes CAPSTONE the first spacecraft ever in a near-rectilinear halo orbit and the first CubeSat to operate at the Moon
First successful CAPS crosslink: CAPSTONE ranges against Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, spacecraft-to-spacecraft, without ground tracking
Six-month primary mission complete after 28 NRHO orbits and 7 maneuvers; the enhanced mission begins
May 2024
Contracted 18-month mission wraps with 83 NRHO orbits, 25 orbit-maintenance maneuvers, and five LRO crosslink demonstrations; the spacecraft flies on as a technology testbed

Extended-mission experiments fly: autoNGC navigates the spacecraft with star-tracker images of the Moon and Earth while the Deep Space Network is busy with Artemis II, and DTN store-and-forward networking delivers every byte across broken contacts
Jun 2026
NASA activities conclude with all primary and extended mission objectives achieved, nearly four years after launch
Jul 2026
Advanced Space keeps flying CAPSTONE as a commercial testbed, station-keeping in the NRHO roughly weekly (as of July 2026)
